# Which files a change touches decides which work it runs (.github/what-changed.sh applies this
# file; CLAUDE.md, "Heavy tests", says when each runs). One entry a line: a path ending in / is
# everything under it, any other path the one file. A group's -not section takes back part of
# it: of all the entries that hold a file, the longest decides. Every entry must exist, and no
# entry is in a group and its -not section both (tests/heavy.rs holds both).
#
# Kept wide on purpose: when unsure whether a file reaches what a group guards, it is in.

# The heavy grids: how a flow's text is translated to steps and run. The translator and the
# core crates it compiles to and runs on, and the server's run engine: all of crates/holon/src
# but what never runs a flow (the commands, the terminal editor, sign-in and who may do what, the
# record's export and check, housekeeping), and its other test files.
[grids]
Cargo.lock
Cargo.toml
rust-toolchain.toml
.github/file-rules.txt
.github/what-changed.sh
.github/workflows/heavy.yml

# The heavy records sweep: how run records are kept, exported, chained and verified. What writes
# a run's line (the run path, its marks for secrets, what it keeps of files and calls), what
# keeps and seals the log, what exports and checks it, and what the check runs again (the core
# crates; the translator, since the sweep's flows are compiled from text).
